questions.q: The total number of three-digit numbers, divisible by $3$, which can be formed using the digits $1, 3, 5, 8$, if repetition of digits is allowed, is&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

Three-digit number to be formed which are divisible by& $3$~using the digits~$1, 3, 5, 8$~and repetition is allowed,

Now taking case~ \left(1\right)$, where all digits are same, we get

\left(1, 1, 1\right), \left(3, 3, 3\right), \left(5, 5, 5\right), \left($8, 8, 8\right) \to $4\text{ways}

Now taking case~\left($2\right)$, where~$2 -$digit are same and one is distinct, we get

\left($5, 5, 8\right) \to $\dfrac{3 !}{2 !} ==3\text{ways,} \left(8, 8, 5\right) \to 3\text{ways}$

Now taking case~\left(3\right)$, where all are distinct, we get

\left(1, 3, 5\right) \to 6\text{ways}, \left(1, 8, 3\right) \to 6\text{ways}$

So, total ways will be~$4 + 3 + 3 + 6 + 6 = 22$

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Total trangles }=\Rightarrow={ }^{\mathrm{h}} \mathrm{C}_3 \\ & \text { Total auadrilaterals }={ }^{\mathrm{h}} \mathrm{C}_4=\mathrm{q} \\ & { }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_3+{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_4=126 \Rightarrow{ }^{\mathrm{n}+1} \mathrm{C}_4=126 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}+1=9 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=8 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{x}^2}{16}+\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{\mathrm{n}}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{x}^2}{16}+\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{8}=1 \\ & \mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1-\frac{8}{16}}=\sqrt{\frac{8}{16}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $n$ is the number of ways five different employees can sit into four indistinguishable offices where any office may have any number of persons including zero, then $n$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Rooms are identical,

So, total ways to distribute $5$ employees into $4$ rooms are:

$5, 0, 0, 0 ⇒ 1$ way

$4, 1, 0, 0 ⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{4 !} = 5$ ways

$3, 2, 0, 0 ⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 10$ ways

$2, 2, 0, 1 ⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{2 ! 2 ! 2 !} = 15$ ways

$2, 1, 1, 1 ⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{2 ! \left(1 !\right)33 !} = 10$ ways

$3, 1, 1, 0 ⇒ \dfrac{5 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 10$ ways

Total $⇒ 1 + 5 + 10 + 15 + 10 + 10 = 51$ ways

questions.q: The number of ways to distribute& $30$ identical candies among four children ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}, {C}_{3}$~and ${C}_{4}$~so that ${C}_{2}$~receives atleast $4$~and atmost~$7$ candies, ${C}_{3}$~receives atleast $2$~and atmost $6$& candies, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& ${C}_{1} + {C}_{2} + {C}_{3} + {C}_{4} = 30$

Now it has given that~$4 \le {C}_{2} \le 7 \text{ and } 2 \le {C}_{3} \le 6$

and~${C}_{1} \text{ and } {C}_{4}$~can take any value.

Finding coefficient of $x^{30}$ in

\left(x^{0} + x^{1} + . . . . . . x^{30}\right) \left($x^{4} + x^{5} + . . . . . . x^{7}\right) \left(x^{2} + . . . x^{6}\right) \left($x^{0} + . . . . x^{30}\right)$

$= \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{31}}{1 - x}\right)$2x^{4} $\$left(\dfrac{1 - x^{4}}{1 - x}\right)$x^{2} \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{5}}{1 - x}\right)$

{Ignoring higher power more than $30}

$= \$left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x}\right)$2x^{4} \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{4}}{1 - x}\rright)x^{2}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{5}}{1 - x}\right)$

$= x^{6}\left(1 - x^{4}\$right)\left($1 - x^{5}\right)\left(1 - x\right)- 4$~$= x^{6}\left(1 - x^{5} - x^{4} + x^{9}\$right)\left($1 - x\right)- 4$

$= \left($x^{6} - x^{11} - x^{10} + x^{15}\right)\left(1 - x\right)- 4$

Required coefficient $= C24 4 + 24 - 1 - C19 4 + 19 - 1$~$- C20 20 + 4 - 1 + C15 15 + 4 - 1$

$= C24 27 - C19 22 - C20 23 + C15 18$~$= 430$

$

$⇒ \dfrac{n\left(n - 1\right)}{2} - n = 99n$

$⇒ \dfrac{n^{2} - n}{2} = 100n$

$⇒ n^{2} = 201n$

$⇒ n = 0, 201$~

$n = 0$~is not possible.

$⇒ n = 201$&

questions.q: The number of ways, in which& $5$~girls and~$7$& boys can be seated at a round table so that no two girls sit together is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$7$~boys and~$5$~girls are to be seated around a circular such that no two girls to be seated together,

Now we know that~$n$~objects can be arranged in a circle in~$( n - 1 ) !$~ways.

Let us first arrange~$7$~boys in circular arrangement in~\left(7 - 1\right) !$~ways.

Now there will be~$7$~gaps.

So let us select any~$5$~gaps out of~$7$~gaps and arrange~$5$~girls in the chosen gaps. This can be done in~$C5 7 \times 5 !$~ways.

Hence, required arrangements are~$6 ! \times C5 7 \times 5 !$

$= 6 \times 5 ! \times \dfrac{7 \times 6}{2} \times 5 !$

$= 126\left(5 !\right)2$.

Therefore, required arrangements are~$126\left(5 !\right)2$

$

questions.q: The total number of $5$-digit numbers, formed by using the digits $1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7$~without repetition, which are multiple of $6$, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given set& \left\{1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7\right\}$

Here sum is~$1 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 7$~$= 24$

So there will be two cases

Case (i) When numbers are~\left\{1, 2, 5, 6, 7\right\}$

Arrangement will be~____2 \text{ and } ____6$

In unit place~$2$~&~$6$~can take place because for multiple of~$6$~number should be even & sum of digits should be multiple of~$3$.

So total way in which remaining number can be taken~will be~$4 ! \times 2$~$= 48$~ways

Case (ii)~When~numbers are \left\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7\right\}$

Arrangement will be~____2$~

So total way in which remaining number can be taken~will be~$4 ! = 24$~ways

Adding case (i)~& case (ii), we get

required~$5$-digit numbers~$= 24 + 48 = 72$

$

questions.q: If the sides $AB, BC$ and $CA$ of a triangle $ABC$~have $3, 5$ and $6$ interior points respectively, then the total number of triangles that can be constructed using these points as vertices, is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that for making a triangle, we require three points, which are not on a line.

Here, we have total& $3 + 5 + 6 = 14$~points out of which~$3, 5, 6$~points~respectively, on~$AB, BC$~and~$CA$~are collinear.

Thus, the total Number of triangles formed

$= C3 14 - C3 3 - C3 5 - C3 6$

$= \dfrac{14 !}{3 ! \cdot 11 !} - \dfrac{3 !}{3 ! \cdot 0 !} - \dfrac{5 !}{3 ! \cdot 2 !} - \dfrac{6 !}{3 ! \cdot 3 !}$

$= \dfrac{14 \times 13 \times 12 \times 11 !}{3 \times 2 \times 1 \times 11 !} - 1 - \dfrac{5 \times 4 \times 3 !}{3 ! \times 2 \times 1} - \dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 !}{3 \times 2 \times 1 \times 3 !}$

$364 - 1 - 10 - 20 = 333 .$

Hence, total number of triangles is~$333 .$

questions.q: The total number of six digit numbers, formed using the digits $4, 5, 9$~only and divisible by $6$, is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

We have to form& $6$~digit number using the digits~$4, 5 \text{ and } 9$~and for number should be divisible by~$6$~which means that the addition of number should be divisible by $3$~and unit place should be even, so~we will make following cases:

Case~ \left(1\right)$~The number is~$444444$~which can be arranged in~$1$~way,

Case~ \left(2\right)$~when the number is formed using the digits~$4, 4, 4, 5, 9$~and last place is fixed with $4$,~that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{3 !} = 20\text{ways}$

Case~ \left(3\right)$~when number is formed using the digits~$4, 4, 5, 5, 5$~and last place is fixed with~$4$, that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 10\text{ways}$

Case~ \left(4\right)$~when number is formed using the digits~$4, 4, 9, 9, 9$~and last place is fixed by~$4$, that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 10\text{ways}$

Case~ \left(5\right)$~when number is formed using the digits~$4, 5, 5, 9, 9$~and last place is fixed with~$4$, that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{2 ! 2 !} = 30\text{ways}$

Case~ \left(6\right)$~when number is formed using the digits~$5, 9, 9, 9, 9$~and last place is fixed with~$4$, that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{4 !} = 5\text{ways}$

Case~ \left(7\right)$~when number is formed using the digits~$5, 5, 5, 5, 9$~and last place is fixed with~$4$, that can be arranged in~$\dfrac{5 !}{4 !} = 5\text{ways}$

Now adding all the cases we get,~$1 + 20 + 10 + 10 + 30 + 5 + 5 = 81\text{ways}$.

$
